extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and respondents in USPTO disciplinary / reciprocal-discipline proceedings; OED staff and USPTO counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural standards for seeking reconsideration of USPTO disciplinary orders in matters processed under the reciprocal-discipline rule (37 C.F.R. § 11.24), including which regulatory provisions apply and service/timeliness considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline framework (37 C.F.R. § 11.24) does not authorize motions for reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: The rules governing reciprocal discipline do not permit or authorize parties to file motions for reconsiderations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a matter is filed and processed pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, there is no express authority in that regulation to grant reconsideration; a party may not obtain reconsideration unless the regulation itself provides for it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of petitions under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions to the USPTO Director under 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(e) govern petitions to the Director in disciplinary matters, but that provision does not apply to reciprocal-discipline proceedings processed under § 11.24 when there is no underlying petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A respondent cannot invoke § 11.2(e) in place of the reciprocal-discipline framework; § 11.2(e) requires an underlying petition context which is absent in reciprocal-discipline cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory framework governing the proceeding controls available remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Because this matter was filed pursuant to, and is processed according to, the regulatory framework for reciprocal discipline, the rules and remedies specified in that framework control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine which regulation (e.g., § 11.24 vs. regulations governing hearing appeals) governs the case; only procedures and remedies authorized by the controlling regulation are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish hearing-appeal rules from reciprocal-discipline rules (37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c) vs § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the USPTO's regulations that govern hearing appeals, including 37 C.F.R. § 11.56(c), the rules governing reciprocal discipline do not permit or authorize parties to file motions for reconsiderations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not import procedural mechanisms from the hearing-appeal rules into reciprocal-discipline matters; consult the specific regulation applicable to the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness requirement for requests for reconsideration (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director argued that the reconsideration request was untimely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reconsideration mechanism exists under the controlling regulation, timeliness rules associated with that mechanism must be satisfied; untimely requests can be dismissed without reaching merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency must follow its own regulations (precedent: Crediford v. Shulkin)
rubrics_metrics.description: "[A]n agency is bound by its own regulations." (Crediford v. Shulkin, 877 F.3d 1040, 1047 (Fed. Cir. 2017)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO cannot grant relief or apply procedures beyond those authorized by its regulations; reliance on agency precedent and regulatory text is required when deciding procedural availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: When procedural authority for relief is absent, merits need not be addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Since there is no provision providing for reconsideration under the reciprocal-discipline regulatory framework, there is no need to address the remaining arguments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A procedural bar (e.g., lack of authority or untimeliness) can be dispositive; deciding procedural availability may obviate the need to evaluate substantive claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal-discipline proceedings depend on the underlying state/jurisdictional discipline order
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint requests exclusion from practice before the USPTO and is predicated upon the January 2, 2020 Order of the Supreme Court of California in State Bar Court No. 14-O-00848, disbarring Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reciprocal discipline is grounded on final disciplinary actions from other jurisdictions; the USPTO action mirrors and is founded upon those external orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate-of-service requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Order certifies mailing by first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the Respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), and email service to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper service of orders and filings in disciplinary matters per § 11.11(a) (including use of most recent address on file and appropriate electronic service), and include a certificate of service documenting compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allegations based on specific disciplinary regulation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Complaint alleges that Respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) and seeks exclusion from practice before the USPTO on that basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and plead the specific regulatory provisions alleged to have been violated (e.g., § 11.804(h)); substantive adjudication will be framed by those cited regulations.
